_comment: Perf ratchet baseline for `make bench`. CI (.github/workflows/perf.yml) runs `make bench` to produce bench-current.json, then compares each metric below against the current value. A metric REGRESSES if current > baseline * (1 + tolerance_pct/100) for direction='lower' (latency, memory), or if current < baseline * (1 - tolerance_pct/100) for direction='higher' (throughput, WPS). To regenerate after a deliberate perf improvement, run `make bench` on the canonical CI runner and copy the resulting bench-current.json values into this file (only the metric values that improved — never grow a baseline value without justification).
_runner: ubuntu-22.04 (sandbox baseline — regenerate on dedicated CI runner for production use)

bench_startup.cold_import.first_run_ms.notes: RETARGET (Phase 2 / master plan §3.4 + §6.2 P-1): now measures worker-startup time (spawn → worker_started stdout), which includes the prewarm phase (onnxruntime + ctranslate2 + numpy/scipy + faster_whisper file-warming). Was 800.0 ms pre-Phase-2 (tray-import). The master plan §3.4 commits to ≤ 600 ms post-migration (25% improvement). The old tray-import measurement is still available via `bench_startup.py --target voice_typer.server.tray`.

bench_startup.cold_import.median_ms.notes: RETARGET (Phase 2): worker-startup page-cache-warm median (was tray-import median). Kept at 300.0 — the prewarm file-warming hits the OS page cache, so the warm median should be similar to the old tray-import median.

bench_startup.cold_import.p99_ms.notes: RETARGET (Phase 2): worker-startup p99 (was tray-import p99). Tightened from 800.0 → 600.0 to match the new first_run target — the worker's prewarm phase is more deterministic than the old torch import, so the p99 tail should be shorter.
